name: Darkshire
summary: Darkshire, formerly known as Grand Hamlet, is a battered settlement in eastern Duskwood. Cloaked in an enduring, unnatural gloom and neglected by Stormwind, the town survives only through the vigilance of the Night Watch and the stubborn endurance of its people.

sections.title: A Town Abandoned
sections.body: Once a peaceful woodland settlement called Grand Hamlet, the village was razed by the Old Horde during the First War and later rebuilt. Its fortune turned truly bitter following the fall of Medivh at Karazhan, whose lingering death throes cursed Brightwood into the shadowy wilderness now called Duskwood. Despite being a nominal holding of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the town hall receives virtually no aid from the crown. Political paralysis in Stormwind City has left the garrison unstaffed and the borders unpatrolled, forcing Mayor Ello Ebonlocke and the local council to administer their own harsh, insular justice in the shadows.

sections.title: The Line in the Dark
sections.body: Surrounded by walking dead from the western graveyards and feral worgen hunting through the woods, Darkshire clings to life along its palisades. The town's primary shield is the Night Watch, a voluntary civilian militia commanded by Althea Ebonlocke. Operating out of the town square and patrolling the pitch-black thoroughfares, these weary sentries keep the town's roads open and turn back the terrors prowling the tree line. Travelers arriving at the Scarlet Raven Tavern find the locals suspicious, frightened, and desperate for any mercenary capable of holding a blade.

faq.q: Why was the town renamed from Grand Hamlet?
faq.answer: The settlement was originally named Grand Hamlet when the region was still the sunny forest of Brightwood. After the Guardian Medivh died at nearby Karazhan, dark magic crept across the woods, blocking the sunlight and raising the dead. As Brightwood decayed into Duskwood, the bleak reality of their cursed surroundings prompted the residents to rename the village Darkshire.

faq.q: Why isn't Stormwind helping defend Darkshire?
faq.answer: Stormwind withdrew its troops from Duskwood amid political turmoil following King Varian Wrynn's disappearance. The townspeople formed the Night Watch to defend themselves against threats the crown was no longer containing.

aliases: who is in charge of darkshire
faq.answer: Civic authority rests with Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the Council of Darkshire, operating out of the town hall alongside town clerk Daltry. Martial defense is led by Ello's daughter, Commander Althea Ebonlocke, who commands the volunteer militia known as the Night Watch.

The Night Watch is a local civilian militia formed out of necessity by Althea Ebonlocke. Because the Stormwind Army will not deploy troops to Duskwood, local townsfolk took up arms to patrol the gloomy roads, secure the borders, and push back ghoul incursions and rogue beasts.
Morgan Ladimore was a veteran who returned after the Third War to find his home ruined and his family missing. His search brought him to Darkshire; local accounts preserve the rest of his story.

angles.text: Darkshire is a stark reminder of the kingdom's fracturing frontier. Alliance heroes will find grateful townsfolk, but also palpable bitterness toward the unresponsive nobility back in Stormwind City.
With the dead rising in every surrounding cemetery and the Light all but forgotten by frightened locals, holy warriors find no shortage of unholy blights to purge around the village perimeter.
